CODwas provided by trained and supervised nonspecialist research assistants called 'ehelpers', using the in-app messaging system. The e-helper team consisted of male Syrian Arabic-native speakers with an educational background in psychology and were refugees. Participants could at any time reach out to e-helpers for help with the intervention, app functionality, technical issues, or other topics, including referral to other services. The in-app messaging feature was data efficient and incurred no additional costs, although it required an internet connection to send and receive messages.
